Nxeon platform (/opt/nxeon), a VPS/game hosting business. This is READ-ONLY research — do not change any code.

The owner wants a large batch of new SEO landing pages: every real game family (all ~40+ in `GAME_FAMILIES`, `lib/games.ts`) crossed with every requested location (Singapore, Southeast Asia, South Korea, Japan, Malaysia, Indonesia, Germany, United Kingdom, India, United States, North America, Canada, Europe, Netherlands, Australia, and similar), e.g. "Singapore Minecraft Server Hosting", "Germany VPS Hosting", "Japan Valheim Server Hosting", plus general "[Location] Game Server Hosting" and "[Location] VPS Hosting" pages. This could be 500+ pages total.

IMPORTANT CONSTRAINT the owner has been told and should already expect from whoever picks up implementation: Nxeon only has REAL infrastructure in two regions — Singapore (APAC) and Falkenstein, Germany (EU). For locations with no nearby real datacenter (United States, Canada, North America, Australia, India, etc.), the copy must be HONEST — framed as "served from our Singapore/Germany network, optimized for low latency to X" — NEVER implying a local server/datacenter presence that doesn't exist. This is a hard legal/ethical requirement, not a style preference.

From a prior session's work (already deployed), I know:
- A `[slug]` dynamic route matrix already exists generating ~107 location-based VPS hosting pages (city/region), built from `components/marketing/locationtemplate/{LocationLanding,data}.tsx` and `lib/marketing/locationLandings.ts`.
- A separate per-game hosting page system exists too — `components/marketing/gamelanding/data.ts` was mentioned as backing ~42 hardcoded `*-server-hosting` pages (one per game family, no location dimension).
- There's a `PricingGrid.tsx` shared component used across many of these templates, and `UseCaseLanding`/`ComparePageLayout`/`MigrateFromPageLayout` are other existing page-template types.

YOUR TASK — investigate and report back, do not write any code:
1. Read `lib/marketing/locationLandings.ts` in full — what's the actual data shape (is it a flat array of location configs, or does it already have per-location metadata like coordinates, nearby-node mapping, "served from" language)? Is the `[slug]` route genuinely dynamic (one page template + a data table), or are there many separate page.tsx files?
2. Read `components/marketing/locationtemplate/LocationLanding.tsx` and `data.ts` in full — what does the actual generated page look like (sections, copy structure, SEO metadata — title tags, meta descriptions, structured data/schema.org markup if any)? Does it already handle the "no local datacenter, served from elsewhere" framing anywhere, or does every existing location page assume a genuinely local presence?
3. Read `components/marketing/gamelanding/data.ts` in full, and find the actual page route/template it feeds (search for where this data is imported and rendered) — same questions: data shape, whether it's genuinely templated, what SEO metadata it produces.
4. Determine: is there already a proven, clean way to build a THIRD dimension — location × game — reusing pieces of both existing systems (e.g., a new dynamic route like `/[game]-server-hosting-[location]` or `/[location]-[game]-hosting`, built from a template that combines both existing data sources), or would this need a genuinely new template component? Look for any existing precedent of a two-axis (game + location) page anywhere already, even a single hardcoded example.
5. Check `app/sitemap.ts` or wherever the sitemap is generated — does it already enumerate the existing ~107 + ~42 pages dynamically from the same data sources? This matters for whether adding a new matrix will automatically get indexed/discoverable, or needs separate sitemap work.
6. Check for any real, structured "nearby node → good-latency countries" mapping already in the codebase (e.g., in `lib/node-regions.ts` or `lib/nx/catalog.ts`, which were referenced in a past session as having real datacenter coordinates and region codes) that could drive an HONEST "which locations can we credibly serve well from which real node" list, rather than a made-up one. Report the real distances/latency reasoning already encoded (if any) so location groupings are defensible (e.g., is Japan actually reasonably close to Singapore, or should its copy lean more on "Germany" for a different reason, etc.) — I don't expect precise ms figures, just what's already structurally present that's honest to build on top of.

Report back concisely but completely — this will directly drive building potentially 500+ new pages, so getting the existing architecture right matters a lot. Include file paths/line numbers for anything you cite.

I now have a complete picture of the architecture. Here's the full report.

## 1. `lib/marketing/locationLandings.ts` (1180 lines)

**Data shape:** a flat, hand-curated array `LOCATIONS: LocationDef[]` (18 cities, lines 81–282) with rich per-location metadata already:
- `region`, `regionLong`, `audience` (prose adjectives), `nearby: string[]`, `hub` (one factual connectivity sentence), and critically **`presence: "datacenter" | "network" | "market"`** (lines 55–63) — a real honesty flag, not cosmetic.
- Only `singapore` and `germany` are `presence: "datacenter"` (lines 83–111) — matching the two real Hetzner/OVH nodes. Everything else is `"network"` (in the network map, no on-site infra) or `"market"` (pure audience target).
- A parallel `REGIONS: RegionDef[]` (lines 785–823) sits one tier up (usa, europe, asia-pacific), each rolling up several `LocationDef`s, with its own `presence` field.
- `SERVICES: ServiceDef[]` (6 entries: vps/game/web/dedicated/forex/reseller) is the second axis multiplied against `LOCATIONS`/`REGIONS` to build `COMBOS`/`REGION_COMBOS` (flat cross-product, `Array.flatMap`, lines 356–362 and 827–833).

**Genuinely dynamic:** yes. `app/(marketing)/[slug]/page.tsx` (single file, 119 lines) is the entire route — it resolves the slug against `findRegionCombo`/`findCombo`, calls `buildRegionLanding`/`buildLanding` to produce a `BuiltLanding` (metaTitle/metaDescription/OG/breadcrumb + a `UseCaseContent` object), and renders it through the shared `<UseCaseLanding>` component. No per-slug files. `generateStaticParams` enumerates `[...REGION_LANDING_SLUGS, ...LANDING_SLUGS]`. Real DB plans (`db.plan.findMany`) feed pricing.

**Already handles honesty framing — yes, thoroughly.** `serverLocationFaq()` (lines 396–407) and `regionServerLocationFaq()` (lines 858–875) branch on `presence`:
- `datacenter` → "Nxeon operates a datacenter in {city}."
- everything else → "Our production platform runs from a Singapore datacenter today with regional build-out underway, so at checkout you'll deploy to the nearest available region." — exactly the framing the owner wants, and it's already the default for 16 of 18 cities and 1 of 3 regions.

Note: **`RESERVED_SLUGS`** (lines 345–352) excludes the 6 Singapore combos from this dynamic system entirely — those are hand-written static pages using a different, richer template (see #2).

## 2. `components/marketing/locationtemplate/LocationLanding.tsx` + `data.ts`

This is **not** what backs the ~107-page matrix. It's a separate, richer, Singapore-only visual template (hero + animated `SeaLatencyMap` + latency bars + peering-fact cards + plans + reviews + closing CTA), originally built as a "preview-only" direction (see the file header, `data.ts` lines 1–14: *"PREVIEW-ONLY sample data... Net-new — touches no live page"*) that was later wired into production for exactly the 6 real, static Singapore pages: `singapore-{vps,game,web,dedicated,forex,reseller}-hosting/page.tsx` (confirmed via grep — all 6 import `LocationLanding` directly, plus `preview/location/page.tsx`).

- It's parameterized by `hero`/`reasons`/`plans` props so each Singapore service page passes its own copy, but the `CITIES` latency-map data (`data.ts` lines 42–49: KL, Jakarta, Bangkok, Hong Kong, Manila, Sydney with real `ms` figures, ISO2 codes, map coordinates) and `PEERING` facts (lines 67–72) are **Singapore-specific and hardcoded** — not parameterized per location.
- SEO metadata (title/meta/OG) is **not** produced by this component at all — each of the 6 Singapore page.tsx files defines its own `export const metadata` separately.
- Every location this template renders assumes genuine local presence (it's Singapore-only, a real datacenter) — it has no "served from elsewhere" branch because it was never meant to represent a non-datacenter city.

**Conclusion: this component is not reusable as-is for the 500+ matrix** — it's bespoke, single-location, and the honesty logic lives in `locationLandings.ts`/`UseCaseLanding`, not here.

## 3. `components/marketing/gamelanding/data.ts` (2812 lines) + rendering

**Data shape:** `PREVIEW_GAMES: Record<string, PreviewGame>` — 40 hand-authored `PreviewGame` objects (rust, satisfactory, palworld, valheim, cs2, …), each with `name`, `headline`, `deck`, `fromPrice`, `accent`/`glow` colors, `worldName`/`region` ("Singapore · sgp1" — hardcoded), `boot` terminal lines, `plans: PreviewPlan[]`, `reasons`, `reviews`. File header explicitly says this is preview/sample data whose numbers were later matched to real prices (see the comment in `rust-server-hosting/page.tsx`: *"real pricing... already matched the PREVIEW_GAMES.rust demo data exactly... see palworld-server-hosting for a case where it had to be corrected"* — i.e. this data can silently drift from real `GamePlan` DB prices).

**Route: NOT a dynamic template.** ~40 separate hand-written `page.tsx` files exist under `app/(marketing)/*-server-hosting/`, each: imports `PREVIEW_GAMES.<key>`, hardcodes its own `export const metadata` (title/description/OG), hardcodes its own `FAQ` array and `RELATED` links, and renders `<GameLandingCombined game={GAME} .../>` (a 1047-line component) plus its own FAQ/related JSX. There is **no per-game data-driven route** — no `[game]-server-hosting/page.tsx` catch-all. Every game page is a fully separate file with duplicated FAQ JSON-LD (`FaqJsonLd`) and Product JSON-LD (`ProductOffersJsonLd`) wiring.

**Location dimension: none.** `region: "Singapore · sgp1"` is a hardcoded display string inside `PreviewGame`, not a parameter — there is no location axis in this system at all today.

`lib/games.ts` line 3 defines `GAME_FAMILIES` with **47 entries** (not ~40+, literally 47, including `stationeers` which the sitemap comment says is deliberately excluded from SEO pages because the product doesn't actually start, and 4 `plutonium*` variants treated as "specialty/community", lower priority, separate from the "flagship grid"). Only 40 have a `PreviewGame` entry and a real page.tsx today.

## 4. Precedent for a two-axis (game × location) page

**None exists anywhere in the codebase.** Grepped for any game+location cross reference (`app/admin/infrastructure`, `DeployView.tsx`, `lib/ipam.ts`, `lib/game-order.ts` were the only hits, all irrelevant — deploy/infra plumbing, not marketing pages). There is no `/minecraft-server-hosting-singapore`, no `/singapore-minecraft-server-hosting`, not even a hardcoded one-off example.

**Building it would need a genuinely new template/route**, but it can cleanly reuse both existing pieces rather than starting from zero:
- **Reuse the honesty engine wholesale:** `LocationDef` (with `presence`), `serverLocationFaq()`, and the `nearby`/`regionLong`/`audience` prose fields from `locationLandings.ts` are exactly the mechanism needed to keep 500+ pages honest — they already encode the "datacenter vs network vs market" distinction per location.
- **Reuse `GAME_FAMILIES`/`PreviewGame`-shaped game facts** (or better, promote real `GamePlan` DB data) for the game-specific half of the copy (RAM sizing, mod ecosystem, slot counts).
- **Reuse `UseCaseLanding` + `PricingGrid` + `FaqJsonLd`/`ProductJsonLd`** as the actual render/SEO layer — this is the proven, genuinely-scaled pattern (`[slug]/page.tsx` already renders 100+ pages through it with zero per-page files).
- The new piece needed is a `buildGameLocationLanding(gameFamily, locationSlug, plans)` copy builder (new file, modeled directly on `buildLanding`/`buildRegionLanding`) plus a new `app/(marketing)/[gameLocationSlug]/page.tsx` (or extending the existing `[slug]` catch-all to also check a third `GAME_LOCATION_COMBOS` map) with its own `GAME_LOCATION_SLUGS` export for `generateStaticParams`. `GameLandingCombined`'s visual richness (art, boot animation) could optionally be kept for a subset of flagship games, but the FAQ/meta/copy engine should follow the `locationLandings.ts` pattern, not the hardcoded-per-page `*-server-hosting` pattern — that pattern doesn't scale past dozens of pages, let alone hundreds, and would duplicate JSON-LD wiring 500+ times.

## 5. Sitemap (`app/sitemap.ts`)

**Partially automatic, partially not:**
- The ~107+ location×service matrix **is** dynamic: `for (const slug of LANDING_SLUGS)` and `for (const slug of REGION_LANDING_SLUGS)` (imported straight from `locationLandings.ts`) — any new `LocationDef`/`ServiceDef`/`RegionDef` added to that file is automatically in the sitemap with zero sitemap changes.
- The ~40 game pages are **not** dynamic — every one is a manually-added literal `{ path: "/rust-server-hosting", ... }` entry in a giant hardcoded `staticRoutes` array (with hand-written comments noting "Wave 3", "Wave 4", "Wave 8/9" additions). Nothing reads `GAME_FAMILIES` or `PREVIEW_GAMES` to build these entries.
- **Implication for the new matrix:** if the new game×location pages are built the `[slug]`-catch-all way (recommended), a `GAME_LOCATION_SLUGS` export plumbed into `sitemap.ts` the same way `LANDING_SLUGS` is gets automatic, low-maintenance indexing for all 500+ pages in one array push. If instead built as hardcoded per-page files (the game-page pattern), someone will need to hand-add 500+ sitemap lines — a real maintenance/scale risk explicitly worth avoiding here.

## 6. Real node/latency data to drive honest groupings

Two real files, consistent with each other:

- **`lib/node-regions.ts`**: `NODE_REGIONS` lists *valid* provider datacenter codes per provider (OVH: sgp1/bhs1/gra1/rbx1/waw1; Hetzner: fsn1/nbg1/hel1/ash1/hil1) — but comments (lines 12–18) are explicit that only `sgp1` (OVH Singapore) and `fsn1` (Hetzner Falkenstein) are **real, live** nodes today; the rest are "real provider codes... listed so the region field has somewhere to grow... add more here as real nodes are added, not speculatively" — i.e. not fabricated, but also not currently active. `CUSTOMER_REGION_LABELS` (lines 47–58) is the exact honest-naming precedent cited in the owner's brief — Falkenstein is deliberately shown as "Germany" to customers. `REGION_COORDS` (lines 91–102) gives **real lon/lat** for every listed code, including the two live ones: `sgp1 {103.85, 1.29}`, `fsn1 {12.35, 50.48}`.
- **`lib/nx/catalog.ts`**: `regionsFrom(nodes)` (lines 66–86) is the load-bearing honesty mechanism for the deploy wizard — it builds the customer-facing region picker **only from Node rows that actually exist in the DB**, filtered further to codes with coordinates. So "how many real locations does Nxeon serve from right now" is a live DB query, not a config file — the file's own header comment states this plainly (*"the wizard offers a region only where a Node actually exists, so the picker can never sell a location we cannot provision in"*). Its local `COORDS` map duplicates the same lon/lat plus a **nominal indicative `ms`** figure per code (sgp1: 12ms, fsn1: 70ms, etc.) explicitly caveated as "NOT a measurement of the customer's own connection."

**What this means for defensible copy groupings:** there is no precomputed "which country is well-served by which node" table anywhere, but the raw ingredients for one exist and are real: two live coordinate pairs (Singapore 1.29°N 103.85°E; Falkenstein 50.48°N 12.35°E) that a great-circle-distance function could honestly rank any requested location against. Rough sanity-check using those real coordinates (not something already computed in the repo, just geography): Singapore is reasonably close to Japan/Korea (~4,600–5,300 km, same general Asia-Pacific hemisphere, no US/EU detour) and clearly the better of the two nodes for Southeast Asia, Japan, South Korea, Australia, and India; Germany is the far-better node for the UK, Netherlands, and other European targets; for the US/Canada, **neither** node is close (both ~8,700–16,000 km away) — those pages should lean hardest on the existing "served from Singapore/Germany, pick nearest at checkout" language rather than imply either node is a good latency story, and copy should probably compare the two nodes' distance rather than assert a false "good ping" claim the way the Singapore-specific `SeaLatencyMap`/`CITIES` bars do for real SEA neighbors. The existing `presence: "market"`/`"network"` distinction in `LocationDef`/`RegionDef` already encodes this instinct correctly (e.g., `usa` region is `presence: "market"`); it just isn't yet driven by actual computed distances — it's manually assigned per entry today, which is fine at 18 locations but will need either a small distance-based helper or continued manual review at 500+ combos to stay defensible.

---

### Bottom line for whoever implements this
- **Location × service** matrix (`lib/marketing/locationLandings.ts` → `[slug]/page.tsx` → `UseCaseLanding`) is the clean, proven, genuinely-scaled pattern — copy it, don't touch `LocationLanding.tsx`/`gamelanding` for the new matrix.
- **Game × service** pages are the opposite: 40 hand-duplicated files, no data-driven route, sitemap entries added by hand — this pattern must NOT be extended to 500+ pages; it would mean 500+ new files and 500+ hand-typed sitemap lines.
- Recommended shape for the new work: a new `buildGameLocationLanding()` copy-builder file mirroring `buildLanding`/`buildRegionLanding`, a new combo/slug table exported for both `generateStaticParams` and `sitemap.ts`, rendered through the existing `UseCaseLanding`/`PricingGrid`/`FaqJsonLd`/`ProductJsonLd` stack, with the `presence`-style honesty flag (and ideally a real great-circle-distance check against the two live `REGION_COORDS` entries) carried straight through from `locationLandings.ts`.
